CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism management

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism presenting for follow-up. Patient initiated testosterone replacement therapy 5 months ago and reports significant improvement in symptoms including increased vigor and improved sleep quality. Patient notes positive effects reflected in improved laboratory values, particularly triglycerides which have decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL, and improved cholesterol. Red blood cell count has increased but remains stable. Currently taking testosterone 1 mL (140 mg) every 10 days, finasteride 2.5 mg daily (half of 5 mg tablet), and cialis 2.5-5 mg daily (5 mg on days he works out, 2.5 mg otherwise; reports currently out of supply). Patient tracking doses with medication calendar. Patient inquired about increasing testosterone to 175 mg but was counseled against this given previous peak testosterone levels exceeding 1,500 ng/mL with associated cardiovascular risks. Also inquired about indole-3-carbinol or broccoli extract for estrogen control; explained that estradiol is not elevated and testing not needed more frequently than annually. Patient is on day 8 of current testosterone cycle, due for next injection Thursday or Friday. Patient reports overall doing well and taking steps to improve his health.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling vigorous with good sleep quality. Denies concerning symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- HIV infection
- Hypogonadism
- History of elevated triglycerides

MEDICATIONS
1. Testosterone 1 mL every 10 days (140 mg)
2. Finasteride 2.5 mg daily (half of 5 mg tablet)
3. Cialis 2.5-5 mg daily (5 mg on workout days, 2.5 mg on other days) - currently out of supply

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works out regularly. Uses Walmart pharmacy. Prefers paper prescriptions. Uses medication calendar to track compliance.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears trim
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no concerns noted
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation, no concerns noted
Remainder of exam: Unremarkable

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (reference <4 ng/mL; previous 0.5 ng/mL last year)
Testosterone: Previously >1,500 ng/mL (peak levels)
Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (improved from 265 mg/dL)
Cholesterol: Improved from baseline
Estradiol: Not elevated
Red blood cell count: Increased but stable

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Hypogonadism: Continue testosterone 1 mL (140 mg) every 10 days. Do not increase to 175 mg at this time. Counseled that peak levels already exceed 1,500 ng/mL with associated increased cardiovascular risk. Discussed dangers of excessive testosterone dosing and connection to serious adverse events.
2. Finasteride: Continue 2.5 mg daily
3. Cialis: Continue current dosing; refill provided
4. Estrogen management: Estradiol not elevated. Offered repeat testing in fall if desired, but not needed more frequently than annually.
5. PSA monitoring: Continue annual PSA checks
6. Prescriptions: Provided paper prescriptions as requested for testosterone, finasteride, and cialis; continue Walmart pharmacy
7. Follow-up: Annual follow-up or as clinically indicated
